scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported Russia interval begins in 1994 after the 1991 Soviet dissolution; the historical 1991 date does not redraw or certify polygons. The Soviet Union and Russian Federation have separate cards.

The 2014 Crimea claim and 2022 invasion are described using UN General Assembly positions; map geometry must not imply international recognition of annexed Ukrainian territory. Chechen civilians and minority languages are not interchangeable with the state.

Shared kitchens/toilets are documented communal-flat examples, not a national norm. Constitutional rights are distinguished from access during economic transition. Original Russian excerpt is from amended constitutional text. Narrative awaits independent review.

proposedOverrides.summary: The Russian Federation emerged from the Soviet breakup in 1991, three years before the imported map begins. It continued the Soviet UN seat and adopted a constitution in 1993. Market transition caused hardship, Chechen wars harmed civilians, and Russian-built hardware helped begin the space station. Its 2014 claim to Crimea was rejected by the UN General Assembly, which also demanded withdrawal after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. Russia continues with many peoples and languages.

identityEvidence.assessment: Imported label/interval confirmed; modern international border accuracy unverified, especially later disputes.
